function.name: get_stock_price
function.description: Get the closing stock price for a specific company on a specified date. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

date.description: Date of when to get the stock price. Format: yyyy-mm-dd.

exchange.description: Name of the stock exchange market where the company's stock is listed. Default is 'NASDAQ'

But note: Jan 1, 2022 was a holiday (New Year's Day). The market closed. So there might not be a closing price. We should handle that. For Jan 1, 2022, the market was closed; the last trading day before was Dec 31, 2021. So the function may return null or error. We need to handle that gracefully.

Similarly, Feb 1, 2022 was a trading day. So we can get actual closing price.

Thus we will call get_stock_price for each combination. Then we will format the results into a table.

We need to use the function tool. We'll do four calls. Let's do them sequentially. We'll store results. Then produce a markdown table with columns: Company, Date, Closing Price (USD). If no data, indicate "Market Closed".
